name: Otilonium

overview.mechanism: Blocks L-type calcium channels in colonic smooth muscle, providing a pharmacologic rationale for spasm relief [[OTI-OBIS]].
uses: Symptomatic IBS treatment studied with otilonium bromide; verify local Spasmomen product instructions rather than transferring a trial regimen into prescribing advice [[OTI-OBIS,OTI-DOSE]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial; 356 patients; 15-week treatment plus 10-week follow-up.
rows.findings: Pain-episode frequency, bloating and patient-rated global efficacy favored otilonium. Pain intensity, responder proportion and quality-of-life scores did not differ. Withdrawal because of symptom relapse during follow-up was 10% versus 27%.
rows.limitations: Different IBS endpoints yielded different findings. Follow-up relapse withdrawal is not a cure or long-term disease-modification endpoint.

rows.design: Double-blind randomized placebo-controlled study; 93 patients; four weeks.
rows.findings: Individual discomfort/pain/bloating measures did not significantly differ between groups. Some bowel-habit and composite discomfort measures favored active treatment. Adverse-event frequency did not differ.
rows.limitations: Small groups, short follow-up, multiple measures; this exploratory trial cannot independently establish an optimal local-product dose.

sources.citation: Randomised clinical trial: otilonium bromide improves frequency of abdominal pain, severity of distention and time to relapse in patients with irritable bowel syndrome. PubMed PMID: 21679214.
Otilonium bromide in irritable bowel syndrome: a dose-ranging randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial. PubMed PMID: 25232263.

common: Short-term trial safety was comparable to placebo; these sample sizes cannot exclude uncommon adverse reactions or define safety in advanced organ impairment [[OTI-OBIS,OTI-DOSE]].

renal: The cited IBS trials do not establish a CKD adjustment or dialysis regimen. Current product-specific renal precautions remain necessary [[OTI-OBIS,OTI-DOSE]].
